grades.question: How are the King and home regions assigned, and where do each player’s initial ten Caballeros go?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle region cards; reveal top for King, each player takes another for home and places Grande. Two Caballeros home, one on first success-track space, seven court; remaining supply provinces.

observed.answer: Reveal a shuffled region card and place the King there. Each player takes another region card as their home region and places their Grande there. Each player’s ten Caballeros are split as two in their home region beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
observed.evidence: Setup: ‘reveal the top card and put the King in that region’; the next card determines home. Ten Caballeros: two home, one on the first success-track space, seven in court.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: Shuffle region cards; reveal top for King, each player takes another for home and places Grande. Two Caballeros home, one on first success-track space, seven court; remaining supply provinces.

grades.question: Who begins playing power cards in the first and later rounds, in what seating direction do others play, and may a played value be matched?
grades.expected_answer: Players choose first-round starter; previous round’s last player begins later rounds; clockwise; no duplicate value in a round.

observed.answer: In round 1, players choose who begins playing power cards. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round begins. Others play clockwise. A power-card value already played that round may not be matched.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure 2: ‘Players choose who begins’ in round 1; later the preceding round’s last-turn player begins; others play clockwise; no value already played this round may be matched.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: Players choose first-round starter; previous round’s last player begins later rounds; clockwise; no duplicate value in a round.

grades.question: What determines turn order and court recruitment, and when is recruitment done relative to choosing an action card?
grades.expected_answer: Descending power value determines turns. Recruit at most pictured Caballeros from provinces into court first, then choose face-up action card.

observed.answer: Turns are taken in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the number shown on your power card from the provinces into your court; recruiting fewer is allowed. Recruitment happens before choosing an action card.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure 3–4: ‘Take turns in descending power-card value’; ‘At the start of your turn recruit up to’ the allowance; ‘After recruitment, choose’ an action card.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: Descending power value determines turns. Recruit at most pictured Caballeros from provinces into court first, then choose face-up action card.

grades.question: If a power card allows recruitment but your provinces lack enough, what alternative is allowed, and which protected locations cannot supply it?
grades.expected_answer: May remove own Caballeros from board to make up difference; not King’s region or Castillo (taboo and no Castillo removal outside general scoring).

observed.answer: If your provinces do not have enough of your Caballeros, you may take your own from the board to make up the difference. The King’s region and Castillo cannot supply pieces for recruitment.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure 3: ‘you may take your own from the board to make up the difference’; the King’s region is taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: May remove own Caballeros from board to make up difference; not King’s region or Castillo (taboo and no Castillo removal outside general scoring).

grades.question: Where may ordinary action-card deployment go, may it be split, and must the full printed allowance be used?
grades.expected_answer: From court to regions adjacent to current King and/or Castillo; split freely; printed number is maximum, fewer allowed.

observed.answer: Ordinary deployment moves Caballeros from your court to regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or to the Castillo, dividing the allowance among destinations as desired. It may be split across those destinations, and the printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
observed.evidence: Actions: deployment is ‘a maximum’; may deploy fewer, including none; move from court to any regions adjacent to the King and/or Castillo, ‘dividing the allowance freely.’

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: From court to regions adjacent to current King and/or Castillo; split freely; printed number is maximum, fewer allowed.

grades.question: May special action and ordinary deployment be done in either order, may either be interleaved with the other, and may the special action be declined?
grades.expected_answer: Either order, each completed wholly before next; no splitting/interleaving. Special action optional, may select card to prevent it.

observed.answer: Yes. Ordinary deployment and the special action may be done in either order. Each must be completed before beginning the other; neither may be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure 4: do them ‘in either order,’ complete one before starting the other, ‘neither may be split or interleaved’; may decline the special action.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: Either order, each completed wholly before next; no splitting/interleaving. Special action optional, may select card to prevent it.

grades.question: What happens to selected and unselected face-up action cards after turns and rounds, and what is exceptional about the King card?
grades.expected_answer: Chosen card laid aside unavailable to later players; remaining face-up cards discarded at round end; King card returns face-up every round, never permanently discarded.

observed.answer: After a player’s turn, their selected action card is laid aside and later players cannot choose it. At the end of the round, discard any face-up action cards left unselected. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure 5: selected card is laid aside; remaining face-up cards are discarded after all turns; the King card ‘is revealed again every round and never permanently discarded.’

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: Chosen card laid aside unavailable to later players; remaining face-up cards discarded at round end; King card returns face-up every round, never permanently discarded.

grades.question: What changes are forbidden in the King’s region, may it still be scored, and what kind of action changes its protected status?
grades.expected_answer: No Caballeros, Grande or mobile scoreboard in/out, even special actions; scoring allowed. King-moving actions move King, changing which region is taboo.

observed.answer: The King’s region is taboo: Caballeros, Grandes, and mobile scoreboards cannot move into or out of it, and special actions do not override this restriction. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
observed.evidence: Protected locations: ‘no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of’ the King’s region; it may still be scored; actions that move the King change the protected region.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: No Caballeros, Grande or mobile scoreboard in/out, even special actions; scoring allowed. King-moving actions move King, changing which region is taboo.

grades.question: When putting Caballeros into the Castillo, what must be announced, how does King location affect entry, and when may they leave?
grades.expected_answer: Announce number added; entry whenever adding/moving Caballeros regardless King; leave only at general scoring.

observed.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros you put into the Castillo. The King’s location does not restrict entry; any or all Caballeros being added or moved may go there. They cannot be removed by an action and leave only during general scoring.
observed.evidence: Protected locations: ‘any or all may go into the Castillo, regardless of the King’s location. Announce clearly how many’; no action removes them; they leave only during general scoring.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: Announce number added; entry whenever adding/moving Caballeros regardless King; leave only at general scoring.

grades.question: List the timing and ordered stages of general scoring, including when destinations are chosen relative to revealing the Castillo.
grades.expected_answer: After rounds 3,6,9: secretly choose destinations first and place disks face down; uncover and score Castillo; reveal disks and move its Caballeros; score board regions in track order.

observed.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: (1) each player secretly selects one destination region other than the King’s region for all of their Castillo Caballeros, placing the disk face down; (2) uncover and score the Castillo; (3) reveal disks and move all Castillo Caballeros to their owners’ selected destinations; (4) score the nine regions in scoring-track order. Destinations are chosen before uncovering the Castillo.
observed.evidence: General scoring stages: after rounds 3, 6, 9; ‘Secretly select destinations before uncovering the Castillo’; then score Castillo, reveal disks and empty it, then score nine regions in track order.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: After rounds 3,6,9: secretly choose destinations first and place disks face down; uncover and score Castillo; reveal disks and move its Caballeros; score board regions in track order.

grades.question: At general scoring, may one player split Castillo Caballeros between regions, choose the King’s region, or keep them in the Castillo; what happens if the King’s region was chosen?
grades.expected_answer: All must go to single disk-selected region, not King’s region; Castillo emptied. Illegal King choice sends own Castillo Caballeros to own court.

observed.answer: A player may not split their Castillo Caballeros: they all go to one destination. The selected destination is normally any board region except the King’s region, and the pieces cannot be kept in the Castillo. If a player selects the King’s region, their Castillo pieces go to their court instead.
observed.evidence: General scoring: each player’s Castillo Caballeros ‘must go to one region’; destination is any board region except the King’s region; if someone selected the King’s region, their pieces go to court; replace the Castillo empty.

grades.reason: All requested material facts match fixed key: All must go to single disk-selected region, not King’s region; Castillo emptied. Illegal King choice sends own Castillo Caballeros to own court.

grades.expected_answer: Three tied leaders each 3 (second rank); next player third rank gets1. Grandes do not count toward majority.

observed.answer: The three players tied for first each score 3 (the second-place value); the player with three Caballeros scores 1 (third-place value). Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.

observed.answer: In a two-player game, only first place can pay; in a three-player game, first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first shifts to second-place value, then the player-count cutoff applies, so neither player scores.
